scope: iPhone control-plane integration without worker mutation authority
winner: sanitized HTTPS GET snapshot backed by the durable mission store

comparison.correctness: high: one deterministic contract derived from durable mission state
comparison.robustness: high: fail-closed on missing auth, missing store configuration, malformed state, or unsupported records
comparison.latency: low for current lab-scale snapshots; one local file read and SHA-256 revision per refresh
comparison.resourceUse: low: no persistent connection or second state service
comparison.regressionRisk: low: no mutation methods and no changes to MissionQueue semantics
comparison.qa: field allowlist, secret-leak regression, deterministic revision, malformed-state rejection, missing/corrupt store coverage

comparison.correctness: potentially high with a separate command protocol
comparison.robustness: medium until phone identity, command fencing, replay protection, and audit semantics are proven
comparison.regressionRisk: high: expands authority surface before Qubes worker readiness is proven
comparison.qa: would require mutation authorization, idempotency, replay, and abuse-resistance suites

comparison.resourceUse: higher: long-lived connections and server lifecycle complexity
comparison.qa: requires reconnect, ordering, duplicate delivery, and lifecycle testing
comparison.result: deferred until polling latency is shown to be inadequate

whyItWon: The phone needs visibility, not worker authority. A strict field allowlist prevents task, result, worker identity, errors, and arbitrary metadata from crossing the control-plane boundary while deterministic revisions support cheap refresh semantics.
failuresAndLessons: The mission queue stores updatedAt as epoch milliseconds while the Swift client expects a String; the API deliberately normalizes it to ISO-8601 rather than leaking storage representation into the client.

The durable store does not persist a per-mission maxAttempts field today, so telemetry currently reports the queue default of 3 unless a persisted record explicitly contains maxAttempts. A future non-default queue policy should persist that policy explicitly before the phone treats this field as authoritative.
A missing store file is equivalent to an empty queue in MissionQueueStore semantics; malformed or unsupported store contents remain fail-closed.
Read-only telemetry is not evidence of real Qubes worker readiness and must not change that readiness gate.
nextGate: run Node contract tests green on this head, then connect the Swift view model to the endpoint and validate an iOS build; real-worker readiness remains gated on an actual Qube-to-Qube qrexec campaign
